_comment: Expectation manifest for lanes' frozen acceptance-checks.
Enforced repo-wide by scripts/evals-all.mjs on every push and PR.
expect "green" = a past fix that must not regress. MUST exit 0.
expect "red"   = a known-failing check (open concern). MUST exit 0 or 1.
A check file missing from this manifest FAILS the gate.
LOCKED (evals/**): improvement loops may never edit this file.

mutations.why: the gate stops scanning for the stopped state, so a T lane falls through to the LIVE branch and the turn is held open on a process the kernel will never schedule
the gate detects the stop and answers it with ctrl+c — a signal that is not delivered until SIGCONT is, so the block names a remedy that frees nothing
the stopped process is never matched back to a lane's checkout, so the gate knows something is stopped and cannot say which lane — which is indistinguishable from not noticing
the stopped row's move goes back to ctrl+c: the state is detected and the lane still cannot be freed, because SIGINT is not delivered to a process the kernel will not schedule
mutations.find: `kill -CONT <pid>` — `ctrl+c` cannot land on a stopped process

mutations.why: the probe stops testing for the stopped state, so flat tokens and flat cost collapse back into one state and a stop is again indistinguishable from a wedge
the probe stops asking ps for process state at all — the one signal herdr cannot supply, and the only thing that separates a stopped lane from a wedged one

dropping superseded entries from the projection is the whole regression: the ledger silently loses its wrong claims, which teaches nothing and hides the error rate from both the user and the next orchestrator
accepting a finding with neither a command nor an explicit unproven marker puts an inference into the record in the same register as a measurement — the exact way a wrong fact becomes durable
a decision with no would_overturn leaves a successor unable to act: they can do something with 'overturned if X still holds' and nothing at all with 'chose option 1'
a blocked lane with no reason shows a block in the Now table with no question attached, which is indistinguishable from work in progress — the failure that let a lane sit idle for an hour
letting anything be acked collapses the one distinction the band rests on: a decision is something the orchestrator resolved for you and you may still overturn, and acking is the user's act alone
mutations.find: if (target.type !== 'decision') die(`${id} is a ${target.type} — only decisions are acked`);

mutations.why: a replacement decision that never reaches decisions/ makes the store and the ledger disagree about what was decided, which is the drift the single-writer rule exists to prevent

the readiness timeout stops being clamped, so a config carrying a lane-runtime number reaches herdr's --timeout and every start dies on invalid_agent_timeout — the defect that produced 0 clean starts in 26
mutations.find:
(( READY_MS > 300000 )) && READY_MS=300000
  (( READY_MS < 3001 ))   && READY_MS=3001

  # Refuse to exceed the declared lane cap
mutations.replace: # Refuse to exceed the declared lane cap

mutations.why: worktree create stops pinning the source repo, so herdr cuts the checkout from whatever the human last focused — three checkouts landed in another session's repo this way
the agent is started without waiting for the pane to reach a shell prompt — the race that answered agent_pane_busy on 8 of 26 starts
mutations.find: wait_shell "$PANE" $(( READY_MS / 1000 )) || die "pane $PANE never reached a shell prompt.
mutations.replace: false && die "pane $PANE never reached a shell prompt.

mutations.why: the readiness predicate stops requiring the foreground process group to BE the shell, so a pane running something else reads as ready
a flag the profile owns goes back to answering "unknown flag", which reads as a typo rather than as a rule
a lane name omitted from the name slot is blamed on the following argument again, sending the operator to the wrong line
mutations.find: [[ "$NAME" == --* ]] && die "the lane name comes first, before any flag:
mutations.replace: [[ "$NAME" == --NEVER* ]] && die "the lane name comes first, before any flag:

mutations.why: start stops requiring --run, so the dispatch record is skipped again and the lane cannot be found — or restarted — after this turn
mutations.find: [[ -n "$RUN" ]] || die "start needs --run <slug>: it names the run whose
mutations.replace: [[ -n "$RUN" || 1 ]] || die "start needs --run <slug>: it names the run whose

mutations.why: the base branch goes back to a hardcoded default, so every repo that does not use it fails at spawn with 'not a valid object name'
an unresolvable base branch is accepted, moving the failure from config time to spawn time where it reads as a broken orchestrator
restart cuts a fresh worktree instead of re-arming the recorded pane, which is start's job and doubles the lane's checkouts
mutations.find:
ARGS=(agent start "$NAME" --kind "$KIND" --pane "$PANE" --timeout "$READY_MS" -- --agent "$PROFILE")
  [[ -n "$MODEL" ]] && ARGS+=(--model "$MODEL")
  [[ -n "$EFLAG" ]] && ARGS+=($EFLAG "$EFFORT")
  [[ -n "$FLAGS" ]] && ARGS+=(${=FLAGS})
  h $ARGS >/dev/null || die "agent start failed for $NAME on $PANE"

  # The branch moved
mutations.replace:
ARGS=(agent start "$NAME" --kind "$KIND" --pane "$PANE" --timeout "$READY_MS")
  h worktree create --cwd "$ROOT" --branch "$NAME-again" --no-focus --json >/dev/null
  h $ARGS >/dev/null || die "agent start failed for $NAME on $PANE"

  # The branch moved

mutations.why: restart drops the profile from the spawn, which is exactly what a herdr /clear does — the defect that ran a whole miniapp track on a default agent with no invariants
mutations.find:
ARGS=(agent start "$NAME" --kind "$KIND" --pane "$PANE" --timeout "$READY_MS" -- --agent "$PROFILE")
  [[ -n "$MODEL" ]] && ARGS+=(--model "$MODEL")
  [[ -n "$EFLAG" ]] && ARGS+=($EFLAG "$EFFORT")
  [[ -n "$FLAGS" ]] && ARGS+=(${=FLAGS})
  h $ARGS >/dev/null || die "agent start failed for $NAME on $PANE"

  # The branch moved
mutations.replace:
ARGS=(agent start "$NAME" --kind "$KIND" --pane "$PANE" --timeout "$READY_MS")
  h $ARGS >/dev/null || die "agent start failed for $NAME on $PANE"

  # The branch moved

mutations.why: restart accepts a lane with no dispatch record, so it re-arms a pane it cannot know belongs to that lane
the raw spawn verbs are no longer denied, so every lane operation can go around the one command that pins the repo, waits for the shell, and records the dispatch
only agent start is caught and worktree create walks through, which is the call that cut three checkouts into another session's repo
the denial stops naming restart, so a lane recovering from a /clear or a wedge is pushed to start, which cuts a second worktree
mutations.find: \$LANE restart <name> --run <slug>                 # re-arm on the lane's existing pane

mutations.why: the escape hatch is removed, so a genuine raw spawn has no way to be recorded as a decision and gets worked around silently instead

a split's workspace_id is recorded again, so a workspace this run never created lands in the file that grants destruction rights — the row that authorized removing the workspace the session itself runs in
worktree create stops owning the workspace it genuinely created, so every legitimate teardown of this run's own lanes is denied as a pane it did not create
the guard stops treating worktree remove as a write, so destroying a workspace needs no ownership at all and the ledger's contents become irrelevant to the one command that deletes checkouts
the record goes back to a PWD-relative path, so a start issued from a subdirectory files it where restart never looks and the lane's recovery path becomes cutting a second checkout
the worktree field is dropped again, so restart's `.worktree` read returns empty: the gone-checkout guard cannot fire and sha_at_restart is measured against the main repo instead of the lane's tree
the record stops naming the lane, so the key every other artifact joins on is missing from the one file that is supposed to make the lane findable
the dispatch record loses `branch`, which is the ONLY key gate-guard joins a branch to a lane by — every push then matches no record and the whole gate silently allows

the dirty listing goes back below the force guard, where --force silences it — and --force is the only way to close a working lane, so the listing is unreachable in the one case where closing abandons work
mutations.find:
if [[ "$DIRTY" != 0 ]]; then
      print -u2 -r -- "lane '$NAME' has $DIRTY uncommitted change(s) in $WT:
mutations.replace:
if [[ "$DIRTY" != 0 ]] && (( ! FORCE )); then
      print -u2 -r -- "lane '$NAME' has $DIRTY uncommitted change(s) in $WT:

mutations.why: the listing names a count but never the files, so the operator is told work exists and not which work — after the pane is closed nothing else points at it
the dirty veto is dropped along with the hoist, trading 'stop before abandoning work' for 'abandon it and mention the files'
the precondition is skipped entirely, so the first lane of a run starts with nothing written down and lane availability is once again the only thing ordering the work
the gate stops reading items.md and accepts a goal restated in prose, so nothing says which item blocks which and there is still nothing to order the work by
mutations.find: (( HAS_ITEM )) || refuse "$PLAN has no numbered items.

mutations.why: a baseline stating an intention rather than an observed exit code is accepted, so every later 'it is green now' is measured against a number nobody took
the gate stops being scoped to the first start and fires on every spawn, which is noise — and noise is answered with a stub file, which is how a gate becomes a ritual
the blind candidate list goes back to dev-first, which is the original hardcode moved one level up: a repo holding both main and dev is told to cut every worktree from dev
mutations.find:
for c in main master dev develop; do
      git -C "$REPO" rev-parse --verify -q "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 && { base="$c"; break }
mutations.replace:
for c in dev develop main master; do
      git -C "$REPO" rev-parse --verify -q "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 && { base="$c"; break }

mutations.why: a checked-out integration branch stops counting as evidence, so cloudflare-os — on dev, origin/HEAD main — is handed main and every lane is cut from the wrong branch
init writes the detected guess into the config instead of leaving it null, turning a heuristic into a decision nobody made

the build exit stops being cross-checked, so gate_passed alone decides — the honour system conductor deliberately refuses, and a reviewer reporting success for a build it never ran walks straight through
the producer is no longer required to differ from the implementor, so a lane gates its own diff — a self-report becoming a gate, which is the rule reported -> verified already refuses
a missing gate artifact reads as a pass, so a lane nobody reviewed leaves the machine and the guard's whole default inverts from deny to allow
--head/-H stops naming the branch, so opening a lane's PR from the base branch resolves to the base, matches no dispatch record, and every PR goes through
a merge that lands ON the base branch stops being treated as outward, so the one merge this guard exists for is the one it ignores
any dod_gate artifact satisfies the frozen definition of done, pass or fail — so a run publishes with criteria it did not meet
the store no longer has to know the lane is committed, so a reviewed lane the run never recorded is pushed — the dark store that let transitions.jsonl stop two days before the session ended
the durable requirement drops to any recorded row at all, so a lane still at 'reported' passes — and a push claims committed, not reported
the transition scan stops filtering by lane, so any other lane's durable row satisfies this one and the predicate stops being about the branch being pushed
a missing transitions.jsonl reads as recorded, so the emptiest possible store — no file at all — is the one case that passes
the gate stops being bound to the sha it reviewed, so a lane can pass, loop back through implementation, commit more, and still present the old PASS — the failure a reshapeable flow makes reachable
a verdict naming no gated_sha is trusted instead of refused, which makes the binding optional and therefore absent for every artifact that omits it

only the FIRST operand is considered, which is the positional read the rewrite removed: `git push -u origin lane-kb` resolves to 'origin', matches no record, and an ungated lane leaves on the ordinary first push
global options are no longer skipped, so `git -C <worktree> push` is not recognised as a push at all — and lanes RUN in worktrees, so that is the normal spelling
a refspec is no longer split, so `git push origin HEAD:lane-kb` and `lane-kb:main` name no lane and walk through
mutations.find: for part in ${(s.:.)o}; do CANDIDATES+=("${part##*/}"); done

mutations.why: gh pr merge stops being a gated verb, so the gate blocks opening a PR and not merging one — it gates the announcement, not the act
a PR number no longer fails closed, so `gh pr merge 12 --admin` merges an ungated lane the hook could not resolve

the repo goes back to being resolved from the session cwd, ignoring -C — measured live: three pushes against a lane with 3 Criticals reached the network, because the orchestrator sits in the main repo while lanes live in worktrees
skip_globals returns through a subshell again, so the -C capture silently does nothing — an assignment inside $(...) never reaches the caller
the stall guard is skipped entirely, so a lane that has yielded nothing across restarts is restarted forever — the shape that ran for a day
progress stops counting: fresh evidence no longer exempts a lane, turning a stall detector into a plain retry counter — the budget conductor deliberately does not use
evidence is no longer filtered to this lane, so another lane's report reads as this lane's progress and the guard never fires
stale evidence written BEFORE the last restart counts as progress, so any lane with any history restarts forever
a subcommand is renamed and the prompt is not updated — the case the derivation exists to catch. A hardcoded list would stay green.
mutations.find:
gate)
  # Dispatch the code gate for a lane, as its OWN lane.
mutations.replace:
reap)
  # Dispatch the code gate for a lane, as its OWN lane.

mutations.why: the agent prompt stops naming the gate verb, so the orchestrator meets gate-guard's refusal with no idea the command exists
a hook is named in the prompt but its refusal is never described, so a filename in a list stands in for a contract
mutations.find: | `gate-guard.sh` | PreToolUse | `git push`, `gh pr create`, `git merge` **onto the base branch** for an ungated lane. See the gate below. |

mutations.why: POLICY-OVERRIDE disappears from the prompt, so three hooks carry an escape the orchestrator does not know exists and routes around silently instead
mutations.find: `POLICY-OVERRIDE` plus a reason on the command line is the stated escape
mutations.replace: `POLICY-NONESUCH` plus a reason on the command line is the stated escape
